attacks.claim: Nothing blocking: images are Ed25519-signed and verified before swap. Keeping 4.7 installable (no anti-rollback increment) is a documented, deliberate choice.
attacks.evidence: Images are signed (Ed25519); the bootloader verifies before swap and keeps the previous image in slot B.

attacks.claim: Home/Away occupancy history is stored in the cloud for 7 days, but the artifact does not say who within an account or household can read it, or how access requests and account deletion handle it.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: authz for Home/Away history across household members; deletion and access handling for occupancy data.

attacks.claim: OTA distribution depends on one existing CDN contract with no stated fallback or exit path.
attacks.evidence: OTA egress: 2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB via existing CDN contract

attacks.claim: At 50% and 100% stages, large numbers of units may install and sync in the same local 3-hour window with no jitter described, creating a cloud load spike.
attacks.evidence: Install window 02:00-05:00 local; the unit waits until no HVAC call is active.

attacks.claim: The 'within monthly commit' claim has no committed figure or retry allowance, and the telemetry increase is unquantified in absolute terms.
attacks.evidence: projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest; within the monthly commit.

attacks.claim: HVAC fault codes gate stage advancement but are not paged, so a relay-fault spike during a multi-day stage relies on someone watching the dashboard.
attacks.evidence: Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1% of updated units in any 6 h window or offline rate rises 0.5 points over baseline.

attacks.claim: Rollback after a successful boot requires the 4.8 OTA client and Wi-Fi reconnect path to work. 4.8 changes reconnect, and revert was tested only on 300 healthy qa-fleet units, so a reconnect regression could strand units.
attacks.evidence: Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path ... Tested on 300 `qa-fleet` units.

attacks.claim: A user who downgrades to 4.7, makes a v1 edit, and re-upgrades silently loses the 8-period schedule they had set. The artifact shows a notice only at downgrade time, not at re-upgrade.
attacks.evidence: When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy, so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule. ABSENT: any user notice when re-upgrade replaces the 8-period schedule.

attacks.claim: The 6% energy claim does not state whether the 2025-26 trial ran this firmware and Away Assist logic, or what the control design was.
attacks.evidence: In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%. ABSENT: trial firmware version and control arm.

attacks.claim: At stage 1, the 0.05% boot-revert threshold is about 3 units out of 6,100, so the gate cannot statistically distinguish an acceptable rate from a bad one.
The 'simplified' message does not identify which periods were dropped, so users cannot check their schedule.
attacks.evidence: The app shows "Some schedule changes were simplified" if v2 had more than 4 periods.

attacks.claim: Away Assist can set Away after 2 h with no motion, which will happen to still occupants (sleeping, reading, sedentary or medically vulnerable people) during scheduled home periods. The artifact offers no override and no false-Away evaluation.
attacks.evidence: sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled "home" periods. ABSENT: false-Away rate for sedentary occupants or an override path.

attacks.claim: The 14-day postpone has no stated forced-install behaviour afterward, so the install time is unpredictable for users.
attacks.evidence: Users can postpone an update up to 14 days from the app.

attacks.claim: Nothing blocking: VoiceOver, TalkBack and 200% text were tested on the new app screens, and French strings were checked.
attacks.evidence: App 9.3 schedule editor and Away Assist screens with VoiceOver, TalkBack, 200% text | Pass

attacks.claim: Occupancy inference may count as sensitive personal information under Canadian rules (for example Quebec Law 25), and the artifact does not show the legal review covered that classification.
attacks.evidence: Privacy notice section 3 updated (legal review LGL-4471).

attacks.claim: Dual-writing v1 and v2 schedules, with cloud-side discard logic, is hidden coupling that will be hard to test across downgrade and re-upgrade paths.
attacks.evidence: 4.8 stores schedules as v2 (8 periods). It also writes a v1 schedule (4 periods) on every edit, keeping the 4 periods closest to ...

attacks.claim: The HIL matrix lists 'no C-wire power stealing' without saying whether power-stealing wiring was tested, and that wiring is common and brownout-prone during flash writes.
attacks.evidence: HIL bench: conventional 1H/1C, 2-stage, heat pump + aux, no C-wire power stealing; rev B/C/D | Pass
